channel.title: News Officina
channel.description: Independent. These outlets are written with AI from public sources; one editor reads and approves what goes out. Each says how it is made on its own About page.

item.title: Europae Laeva: British police arrest serving US soldier on suspicion of spying for Russia
item.description: The 41-year-old was held under the National Security Act near Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps headquarters in Gloucestershire, and faces possible charges from both Britain and the US Army.

item.title: Attacotti: US soldier arrested in England on suspicion of spying for Russia
item.description: The 41-year-old was detained near Gloucester under the National Security Act 2023 and remains in custody at a London police station. The FBI director said the case involves allegations of espionage, which can carry a life sentence before an American military court.

item.title: Europa Surgit: US soldier arrested in England on suspicion of spying for Russia
item.description: Counter Terrorism Policing detained the 41-year-old near Gloucester on 10 November under the National Security Act 2023, with police and the FBI working together on the case.

item.title: Europae Dexter: US soldier at Nato HQ in England arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia
item.description: The 41-year-old, detained near Gloucester under the National Security Act 2023, was posted at Imjin Barracks, home of Nato's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps. He faces possible charges from both British authorities and the US Army, which can carry life imprisonment.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: French cyber agency blames Iran's Revolutionary Guard for shop fridge attack
item.description: The cyberattack forced refrigeration at about 700 retail sites into high temperatures and destroyed the stock. The agency will ask European partners for new sanctions on Iranian entities.

item.title: Europa Surgit: EIB and investors pledge €10bn for European scale-ups
item.description: Seven member states and the EIB Group agreed the first closing of the Tech Champions fund-of-funds, aiming to mobilise up to €80 billion in venture capital.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Italy to offer Ukraine access to two military radar satellites
item.description: Defence Minister Guido Crosetto takes the thirteenth aid package to the Copasir committee on 10 November, as Washington limits its own satellite support to Kyiv.

item.title: Europae Laeva: EU and investors pledge over €10 billion to help European tech firms grow global
item.description: The EIB Group, 15 institutional investors and seven member states have pledged over €10 billion and hope to mobilise up to €80 billion in total, from a first closing of around €2 billion. The money is a pledge, not cash, and the European Commission calculated EU venture funding was about 84 percent below the American level in 2024.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: US, Ukraine and Russia open first talks since February in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff mediate two days of talks on security guarantees and territory, while Russian officials keep European representatives out of the main negotiations.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Moscow bars Europe from US-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Kushner and Witkoff mediate the first direct negotiations since February, as EU leaders decide this week who speaks for Europe. European security advisers remain outside the room.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Italy to give Zelensky's troops access to its radar satellites in thirteenth aid package
item.description: Defence Minister Guido Crosetto will present the package to the security committee Copasir on 10 November and propose extending arms supplies into 2027, as Salvini proposes halting arms and money for Ukraine.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Hungarian media report Viktor Orbán's brother Áron detained in visa fraud raids
item.description: Four people were held in Budapest, Fót and Dunakeszi over a scheme that charged Vietnamese citizens recruitment fees for visas to reach Western Europe. Viktor Orbán called the investigation a witch-hunt against him.

item.title: Europa Surgit: AfD split over ICE criticism as Chrupalla clashes with Weidel
item.description: Chrupalla calls for broader support on migration policy, while Tritschler pushes to copy US deportations. The dispute could shape whether Remigration stays a campaign theme.

item.title: Europae Laeva: Republican Massie files eight impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Hegseth
item.description: The Kentucky congressman accuses Hegseth of waging war on Iran without Congress's approval and of unlawful strikes he says killed hundreds of civilians. House Speaker Mike Johnson calls the move a political trick.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Hackers hit freezers at 700 French supermarkets, Paris blames Iran
item.description: France's Cyber Crisis Coordination Centre named Iran's Shahid Kaveh cyber unit in a report on Monday. One German store owner says he threw away goods worth over 360,000 euros.

item.title: Europa Surgit: Europe has one seat at the table. It must speak with one voice.
item.description: Russia, Ukraine and the United States meet in Abu Dhabi over Ukraine's post-war order. Our leverage, from sanctions to reconstruction, sits in Brussels, so EU leaders in Dublin must agree on one negotiator with a written mandate.

item.title: Leo Batavus: French minister Barrot calls Mélenchon a spokesman for the Kremlin
item.description: The foreign minister said Mélenchon's call for a vote in Donbas disqualifies him from office, and argued the EU budget, not French taxpayers, should carry the cost of backing Ukraine.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Crowd attacked National Guard base near Kyiv after torture-chamber fakes
item.description: Police used tear gas after about 200 people attacked a National Guard facility. Officials say the building was housing, not a prison, and Polish-language outlets spread the false claims.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: Karasin says no agreement exists for Europeans to join the Abu Dhabi talks
item.description: Karasin called French plans of attendance wishful thinking, while Kallas says any agreement the EU is not party to will not be implemented. Costa has put EU participation on the agenda of Friday's informal leaders' meeting in Dublin.

item.title: Europae Dexter: Russia denies Europe a seat at Abu Dhabi talks set by Washington without it
item.description: According to Politico and Euronews, the EU will send officials to parts of the negotiations, but Moscow says no agreement allows it, and the format was agreed by Russia, Ukraine and the United States alone. Kaja Kallas has said the EU will not implement any deal it is not party to.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: EU to take part in Abu Dhabi trilateral talks
item.description: Commission and Council officials will represent Europe in the two-day meetings on November 10 and 11. What is decided there touches Black Sea shipping.

item.title: Attacotti: At least 20 migrants dead after two boats found off southern Crete
item.description: The Greek coastguard rescued 46 people from the two boats and two people are missing, while Frontex teams picked up dozens more on Monday. The deputy migration minister said cooperation with eastern Libya was gone and flows had increased as a result.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: At least 20 dead in two boats off Crete as minister plans EU return hub initiative
item.description: The Greek coastguard rescued 46 survivors from two boats south of Kali Limenes, and Frontex teams picked up about 87 more on Monday. Deputy Migration Minister Sevi Voloudaki says the migration minister will present an initiative with other member states within days.

item.title: Europa Surgit: At least 20 dead in two migrant boats off Crete, two arrested
item.description: The Greek coastguard and Frontex pulled survivors from four boats south of the island between Saturday and Monday, including a toddler taken to hospital. Frontex named the eastern Mediterranean the EU's busiest route in October.

item.title: Europae Dexter: At least 20 dead off Crete as minister says Libya deal no longer holds
item.description: Shipping Minister Sevi Voloudaki says cooperation with eastern Libya has broken down and warns of stricter measures if the EU's return-hub initiative fails within days. Frontex aircraft spotted two further boats south of Crete, with roughly 47 and approximately 40 people aboard.

item.title: Leo Batavus: At least 20 dead in two boats off Crete, minister plans EU return hubs
item.description: Frontex says the Libya-to-Crete corridor is now the busiest part of the eastern Mediterranean route, with about 31,800 crossings so far this year, 15 percent fewer than in 2025.

item.title: Nuntii Europae: Russia says no agreement for Europe to join Abu Dhabi talks with Ukraine and US
item.description: Grigory Karasin of the Federation Council dismissed France's plans to attend as wishful thinking on 9 November. Ursula von der Leyen says the European Union will still be represented alongside its partners.

item.title: The Harbour Ledger: Hackers say stolen Rosstat data shows 450,100 Russian military deaths
item.description: The claim rests on leaked death certificates that Rosstat says were not compromised. At least 168 public datasets have vanished from the agency's collections.

item.title: Attacotti: Ten JEF countries sign naval partnership pact to deter Russian threats
item.description: The British-led agreement commits the navies of Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the UK to interchangeable forces, commanded from Northwood in London. Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre called it a response to American calls for allies to carry more of the burden.

item.title: Europa Patriarum: Ten northern countries sign naval partnership pact led from Britain's Northwood
item.description: Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom sign the agreement, which keeps the forces under national authority. The United States is not part of it.
